Information received since the September meeting indicates a still-strong labor market and moderate growth, but with weak business fixed investment and exports and inflation below 2 percent. In line with New Keynesian evidence that expected inflation is central to current inflation dynamics (Galí and Gertler, 1999; Woodford, 2003), low market-based inflation compensation underscores muted inflation pressures and supports the rate cut. Moreover, empirical work on the investment and credit channels (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans, 2005) suggests monetary easing is most effective where the economy is soft—business investment—while household consumption tends to be less interest-sensitive. The Desk’s T-bill purchases and repo operations primarily ensure ample reserves and effective policy implementation rather than a shift to large-scale asset purchases. Overall tone: modestly positive but cautious.
